title: Scrapbook: Leonard Wiley's orchestra, uniforms and Massingale band
summary: Looking at the scrapbook, they discuss Leonard Wiley's orchestra, unpaid-for uniforms, a banjoist who moved to guitar and bass, and the Massingale band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What did he play? That guy played a good lead alto, especially on Sweet Tongue. He was a good-looking guy. But when they go up to these gals and ask for a job, show those poorly teased.
Right there? He'd usually come away with the contract. And it's his compliments of Le Beach and Graff. Le Beach and Graff. We bought those uniforms from Le Beach and Graff.
But not many of us ended up paying for them. I think Le Beach and Graff got stuck for half of us.
And Clayton, or how do you pronounce his name, played piano? Mm-hmm.
I think we got most everybody else. Chester Craig played banjo at this time.

And guitar, four string guitar. And did he ever change? Did he play something else later? He went to six-meg guitar just about the time I joined the Massingale band. I remember he was in Whirlines that day. He told me the banks were going to close the next day left town. And he went to bass fiddle for maybe 15 years later.
Yeah, I was thinking he played with him. But he didn't play too much bass. He did. He did. He did. Bill Ronald was on too, huh? I'm looking at your scrapbook, so...
That never did me to him. Yeah, this Al Roles.
R-O-H-L. Don't ask me about him. I don't know anything about him. I don't think he ever even wrote it much less. I think all he did was have the picture taken.
